![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/68c8794b1939eb40d6927c5c0f354ce9d5842c7b2fb7949be14c29bd28f10486.png)

The Venn diagram shown above represents two events $A$ and $B$ and the probabilities of each event. Calculate $P(B|A).$
question.worked_solution:
To compute $P(B|A),$ we need to ask, "what is the probability of $B$ occurring given that $A$ has occurred?"

Since we are assuming that $A$ has occurred, we only consider the events inside $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/56a6299b9db053fe3ab235c2cc98f7dfdb849beb37d3f2987026a6f89aa4191b.png)

The probability of event $A$ occurring is

$$
P(A)=0.2+0.05=0.25.
$$

Now, $P(B|A)$ can be interpreted as the proportion of $B$ that lies inside $A,$ relative to the size of $A.$ So, we have

$$
P(B|A)=\frac{0.05}{0.25}=0.2.
$$
